title: De novo design of proteases - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Two Nature papers (Choi and colleagues; Chen and colleagues) report machine-learning-based de novo design of cysteine proteases and metalloproteases, with one group using an RoseTTAFold diffusion variant to obtain catalytically active designs that also work in mammalian cells.

themes.theme: ML enzyme design crosses a hard threshold

insights.claim: De novo design of proteases has been a standing hard case for computational protein design because of the biochemical complexity of their catalytic sites.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Progress here is a proxy for whether AI protein-design platforms can move beyond binders to true catalysts.
insights.locator: De novo design of proteases remains particularly challenging

insights.claim: Two separate Nature papers, from Choi and colleagues and Chen and colleagues, report de novo designed cysteine proteases and metalloproteases built with machine-learning tools.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Two independent groups reaching the same milestone suggests the capability is generalizing, not a one-off result.
insights.locator: Reporting in two separate papers in Nature

insights.claim: Choi and colleagues used RoseTTAFold Diffusion 2 for Molecular Interfaces (RFD2-MI), a diffusion model version tuned for enzyme active sites and protein-protein interfaces.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Task-specialized versions of generative structure models, not general ones, are delivering the hardest wins; watch platform companies building on this lineage.
insights.locator: Choi and colleagues used a version of the RoseTTAFold diffusion model

insights.claim: Of 69 computational cysteine protease designs, 13 were catalytically active against their target peptide sequences, and the active designs adopted folds distinct from natural cysteine proteases.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A roughly one-in-five hit rate on a previously intractable class is the kind of yield metric to track as design models improve.
insights.quote: The authors generated 69 computational designs of cysteine proteases and found that 13 were catalytically active

insights.claim: The designed proteases remained enzymatically active inside mammalian cells, not only in isolated assays.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Activity in cells is the gate for therapeutic or cell-engineering use cases rather than purely industrial enzymes.
